title: CHAPTER 2: GAMING THE SYSTEM THE SOCIAL SORTING APOCALYPSE

segments.line: Within two days, people found cruel ways to use the visible timers against each other.
Bosses checked foreheads during job interviews
and refused to hire anyone with under a year left.
Banks would not approve home loans for couples whose digital clocks showed less than five years.
Pip watched his best friend Mo land a huge promotion at their busy accounting office. Mo had forty-two peaceful years on his forehead, so the manager
Meanwhile, dating apps added a filter so people could hide users with short timers completely.
Landlords kicked out tenants whose displays turned yellow, because they feared broken pipes or missed rent.
People with low clocks were treated like walking human bombs ready to explode at any moment.
Store clerks watched them nervously, and strangers crossed the street just to stay away from them.
Pip wore a thick winter hat to work, but the glowing red light shone right through. His
timer dropped below four days, and every small move felt like stepping on thin ice. He
wondered if one wrong word would ruin his job before the weekend even started.
The social pressure was growing fast, and nobody in the city felt safe around him anymore.
Even his oldest friends made polite excuses whenever he
asked to hang out after work.
